nodes.name: Electrode Preparation and Connection
nodes.procedure: Ni and Co-based catalyst films were prepared on conductive substrates (FTO glass, Ni foil, and Ni foam). Different types of electrode holders (alligator clip, Ti clip, and Pt clip) were used to connect the electrodes to the potentiostat.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS detected contact impedance as a high-frequency semicircle (10^4 - 10^5 Hz) and allowed distinguishing between solution resistance (Ru,EIS,1) and total uncompensated resistance (Ru,EIS,2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contact impedance can be detected through EIS, appearing as a semicircle on the Nyquist plot ... in the high-frequency region (10^4 - 10^5 Hz)

nodes.characterization_summary: CV was used to identify Ni2+/3+ redox peaks (~1.36 V) and calculate redox charges (Qa, Qc). Results showed that a higher degree of iR compensation increases measurable redox charge, especially for nanoporous Ni foam, by alleviating electron trapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests using Ni-based electrodes ... a higher degree of iR compensation alleviates the electron trapping phenomenon, resulting in greater utilization of the redox active sites and consequently increasing the measurable amount of redox charge.

nodes.characterization_summary: CI method measures uncompensated resistance (Ru) via DC technique. It was found to overestimate Ru in the presence of contact impedance at the holder/substrate interface and caused distortion of redox peaks due to in situ scan rate variations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The DC technique-based current interruption is used for the CI compensation method ... this overestimation of Ru,CI can be attributed to the presence of a small contact capacitance ... CI showed a variation in the actual scan rate near the redox peak.
